why: The phone as each variant run has it (WORKLIST P0.86): each name's adb shell commands set before the run touches the phone and put back once it ends, so nothing outlives its run. Where the phone's own value is not a fixed default, `read` takes it first (the last word of its answer, which must match `answer`) and a reset's {was} puts it back. `ready`, for a setting the system takes a while to apply, is asked until it answers yes (exit 0). `flows`: the run takes every flow before the route walk, on three machines; every other variant walks the routes alone, on one. `judges`: what else fails the run on that phone (cut-text: e2e/cut-text-judges.mjs). run-flows.sh runs them (e2e/variants.mjs); variants.test.ts holds every one to a setup, a reset and a reason. `device`: the emulator a variant runs on, when not the one every other run has (below).

device.why: The emulator every run is on unless its variant names its own: a Pixel 6 on Android 14, the image kept in the cache, with 4 GB of memory.

plain.why: The phone as every run has it: the walk's captures every other variant is read against.

motion-on.why: Android's transitions and animations at 1, as most members have them: every other run has them at 0, which React Native and Reanimated read as Reduce Motion. The window animation stays 0, because one holds injected keys. Its walk is still until it has signed in (`stillToSignIn`, e2e/walk-routes.mjs): the signed-out screens keep their own motion, and the driver, waiting for a settled screen, took five minutes over one tap there (nightly 41187219004); so the two routes a guest sees are captured still, and the launch with motion on stays the per-push probe's (run-flows.sh). Its moments are taken still too (`stillForMoments`): a moment is taken for its screen, never its motion, and the calendar's four taps through a moving sheet ran the walk out of its twenty minutes (41284557912).

largest-text.why: The largest text Android offers a member (font scale 2).

bold-text.why: Bold text, as Android's accessibility setting gives it. Its cut text is not judged here: React Native measures a Text with a paint that does not carry this setting while Android draws with it, so every measure the app can make of its own lines is wrong at bold text (runs 39004285239, 39010071533, 39016139854: "E2E_WRITER", drawn whole, measured cut every time). What is cut at bold text is read from the screen itself, by WORKLIST P2.7's position reader.

narrowest.why: The narrowest width a member's phone can be, under 320 dp: the emulator's 1080 px at density 560 is 308 dp.

three-button.why: Android's three-button navigation bar, taller than the gesture bar every other run has.

right-to-left.why: The phone in Arabic (Iraq), as a member who reads Arabic has it: Android lays every app out right to left. The language is taken as the Settings app gives it, while the system runs (e2e/phone/HouseLocale.java, which the workflow builds and run-flows.sh puts on the phone), and the one the phone had is put back the same way. Never by restarting the system: `setprop persist.sys.locale; stop; start` lost the emulator from adb in nightly runs 41187219004 and 41427745512.

dark.why: The system in dark mode. The emulator every other run uses is in light mode (run 39013202388 read "no" before a light run set "no", so that run changed nothing): the plain run is the light system, and this one the dark, so the app is seen in both. The app keeps its own grounds either way. The mode the phone had is read first and put back.

tablet.why: Android 16 on a tablet (API 36, the Pixel Tablet's 2560 by 1600 at density 320: 1280 by 800 dp), held on its side as it rests. Android 16 ignores an app's portrait lock on a screen 600 dp or wider for an app targeting SDK 36, as this one does, so the app runs on its side here as it will on every such tablet and open foldable, each page and sheet held to the reading column. The rotation the phone had is read first and put back.

device.diskWhy: Its data partition, named so its need is known: the emulator asks 1.8 times it free (7.2 GB), and e2e.yml makes that room on the runner before it starts (runs 41175522858 and 41193708096 had 3.2 GB).

pages-16k.why: Android 15 on 16 KB memory pages (WORKLIST P4.29): phones from Android 15 on may run with 16 KB pages, and a native library built for 4 KB ones fails to load there, so the app crashes at its start or when it first reaches that library (MMKV, SecureStore, Reanimated, Skia). Its own system image (Android 16's google_apis_ps16k), every flow on it: the start, the sign-in, the Archive's lock (MMKV and SecureStore) and the critical path. Nothing on the phone is set; the run is that phone only when the phone says its page is 16384 bytes (ready), and stops if it never does.

device.why: Android 16's image with 16 KB pages for x86_64, which the runner's emulator runs. Android 15's (an August 2024 build) crashed inside its own runtime's JIT compiler, with no frame of the app's (run 43019767529: SIGSEGV in libart.so, art::jit::Jit::CompileMethodInternal), so its failures were the image's, not the app's.
device.ramWhy: A system on 16 KB pages holds more memory for the same work: in 4 GB it ran out at its start, killed 187 processes and then died itself, taking the app with it (run 42969525169), where the plain phone killed none. Every phone shipped with 16 KB pages has 8 GB or more; the runner has room for 6.

links.why: Every address as a stranger, by a bad id and warm (WORKLIST P4.21): the plain phone, walking e2e/links.json instead of the routes. Each member's door is signed in from and must land on its own screen, never the Lobby; each id route, malformed and missing, says its screen's words, never an empty page or 'could not reach'; each route opens with the app running.
